methodology: JalDrishti Multi-Criteria Groundwater Risk Engine - Sensitivity & Robustness Audit

test_1_boundary_sensitivity.findings: Lowering the critical threshold to >=5 (Scenario B) expands CRITICAL by 151 blocks (+35.3%), primarily absorbing borderline WATCH blocks with moderate depletion. Raising the critical threshold to >=7 (Scenario D) contracts CRITICAL by 123 blocks (-28.7%), demoting all score=6 blocks to WATCH. Raising the SAFE threshold to <=3 (Scenario C) causes 768 WATCH blocks (14.21% of total) to fall into SAFE, revealing that score=3 is an active boundary separating stable blocks from emerging depletion. No SAFE block ever jumps to CRITICAL in any scenario.

test_2_trend_sensitivity.findings: Linear long-term trend classifications exhibit exceptional robustness against small threshold perturbations. Perturbing the major 0.25 m/yr threshold by ±0.05 m/yr alters only 13 to 21 blocks (0.24% to 0.39% of total). Perturbing the severe overdraft 0.50 m/yr threshold to 0.60 m/yr alters only 5 blocks (0.09%). Perturbing the 0.10 m/yr boundary alters 22 to 41 blocks (0.41% to 0.76%). In all cases, <0.8% of blocks change classification, proving that trend thresholds are free of artificial cliff effects.

test_3_forecast_sensitivity.findings: CRITICAL classifications demonstrate high stability against forecast boundary shifts of ±0.25m. A +0.25m tightening demotes only 24 CRITICAL blocks (5.6% of CRITICAL), retaining 94.4% of CRITICAL blocks. A -0.25m relaxation elevates 28 WATCH blocks to CRITICAL, while demoting 0 baseline CRITICAL blocks. Most fluctuations occur between SAFE and WATCH near the 0.10m / 0.35m boundary.

test_4_depth_sensitivity.findings: Contextual depth thresholds (15/35m vs 25/45m) impact <0.8% of blocks across the repository (17 to 43 blocks). Because depth acts exclusively as an amplifier conditioned on active depletion, depth never independently creates CRITICAL. All 4 sanity checks remain 100% satisfied across all depth perturbation scenarios.

executive_verdict.verdict: ROBUST ENOUGH TO PROCEED TO PRODUCTION INTEGRATION, WITH THRESHOLDS TREATED AS ENGINEERED DECISION RULES RATHER THAN SCIENTIFICALLY VALIDATED GROUND-TRUTH LABELS.
executive_verdict.rationale: The JalDrishti risk scoring engine demonstrates strong robustness under the tested parameter and threshold perturbations. 73.45% of blocks are completely invariant across the 10 final sensitivity stress-test scenarios, and 84.63% are invariant under physical measurement noise. Baseline CRITICAL classifications are secure: 90.19% remain CRITICAL across all physical stress tests, and exactly 0.00% ever collapse to SAFE. The hydrological guardrails provide a reliable safeguard that prevents false-alarm or non-physical classifications.
executive_verdict.fragility_analysis: 1. Score 3 boundary (SAFE <=2 vs <=3): 768 blocks sit at composite score=3. Shifting SAFE cutoff to <=3 causes 14.21% of the repository to switch. Retaining score=3 in WATCH functions as an engineered decision rule to capture emerging depletion (e.g. moderate drop + slight trend). 2. Score 6 boundary (WATCH 5 vs CRITICAL 6): 123 blocks sit at score=6. Raising cutoff to >=7 drops CRITICAL by 28.74%, while lowering to >=5 adds 151 blocks. Score 6 establishes an engineered operational cutoff separating converging multi-criteria stress from single-factor warning. 3. Trend threshold 0.25 m/yr is exceptionally solid: only 0.24% to 0.39% of blocks fluctuate under ±0.05 m/yr perturbations.
